prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Name & Claim Your Desktop Pet", "Give your companion their official desktop name to seal your adoption.", "Pet Name", "Official Pet Adoption"]
1: ["How to Interact with Your Pet", "Click and drag to move your pet around screen edges. Right-click for quick actions and settings."]
2: ["Preparing Your Pet's Desktop Home", "Your companion is getting ready to jump onto your screen!"]
3: []
4: ["Signing in links your pet securely so you never lose your companion or custom features.", "Cloud Save Protected"]
5: ["Generation usually takes under 2 minutes. Stay tuned!"]
6: ["Ready to Jump onto Your Desktop!", "Click below to release your new companion onto your screen.", "Release Pet to Desktop"]
7: ["Feel free to minimize this window. We'll send a system alert when your pet is ready!"]
8: ["For best results, upload well-lit photos with your pet facing forward."]
9: ["Save Your Companion to Your Account", "Sign in to protect your pet's progress, custom features, and access across devices."]
